commit.message:
[inductor] Fix the device of a returned cpu constructor under cudagraphs (#199007)

`ConstructorMoverPass(allow_outputs=True)` rewrites a cpu constructor's `device` kwarg even when that tensor is returned, so under `mode="reduce-overhead"` a compiled function that builds a cpu tensor hands back a cuda one. `allow_outputs` exists for the cpu scalar *input* path from #154464, which is safe because it rewrites uses and skips the output use; a constructor has no such protection, since its kwarg is mutated in place.

This excludes output-reaching constructors, but not placeholders, leaving #154464 alone. Implicit factories are affected too: AOTAutograd materializes `device=cpu`, so a returned `torch.zeros(4)` moved as well.

Fixes #197088

## Test plan

`test_output_failure_cudagraphs` covers the repro and a returned cpu chain; `test_simple_cudagraphs` pins that a constructor consumed only by a gpu op still moves. A/B on a GB200 (CUDA 13.4) by flipping the installed `post_grad.py`: five returned-cpu-tensor cases come back on `cuda:0` before and `cpu` after, with `cudagraph_skips` still 0 wherever there is a gpu output. The file's 10 tests pass, `test_multi_gpu` skipped for want of a second device.

<details>
<summary>Configuration matrix on pristine torch, device of each returned tensor</summary>

```
=== new_zeros(device=cpu)                       eager: cpu
  inductor default                   cpu                      skips=0 ok
  cudagraphs                         cuda:0                   skips=0 MISMATCH
  reduce-overhead                    cuda:0                   skips=0 MISMATCH
  cudagraphs, no partition           cpu                      skips=1 ok
  cudagraphs, allow_outputs=False    cpu                      skips=1 ok

=== arange returned                             eager: cpu, cuda:0
  inductor default                   cpu, cuda:0              skips=0 ok
  cudagraphs                         cuda:0, cuda:0           skips=0 MISMATCH
  reduce-overhead                    cuda:0, cuda:0           skips=0 MISMATCH
  cudagraphs, no partition           cpu, cuda:0              skips=1 ok
  cudagraphs, allow_outputs=False    cpu, cuda:0              skips=0 ok

=== pin_memory=True                             eager: cpu
  every configuration                cpu                              ok
```

`zeros next to gpu out` and `cpu chain to output` behave as `arange returned`. `pin_memory=True` is immune everywhere because a cuda tensor with `pin_memory=True` is not constructible, so the pass cannot rewrite the kwarg.

The bug needs `graph_partition`: with it off, the device is already correct because Inductor declines cudagraphs for the graph instead (`skipping cudagraphs due to cpu device`).

</details>

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/199007
Approved by: https://github.com/kshitij12345, https://github.com/eellison
